bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Epidemiologist Salary Conversion

When you search for an **epidemiologist salary**, you often see an hourly rate or an annual figure. Converting between them is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. For example, an hourly rate of $50 gives an annual gross of $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. This formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates or allowances.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The national minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week, according to the Fair Work Commission. However, most epidemiologists are covered by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award [MA000027], which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for this award, including current minimum rates and allowances. You can check the pay guides for the exact classification that applies to your role. For a professional epidemiologist, the hourly rate is typically above the national minimum, often ranging from $40 to $60 per hour depending on experience and location.

### Casual Loading for Epidemiologists

If you work as a casual epidemiologist, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of your base hourly rate. This loading is paid instead of entitlements like paid leave. For instance, if your base rate is $50 per hour, the casual rate becomes $62.50 per hour. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that casual loading is added to the minimum wage. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the “casual loading” box to automatically add 25% to your base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the calculator applies it on top.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is a key part of your total remuneration. Employers must pay 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, on top of your salary. The super guarantee is capped at a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an epidemiologist earning $98,800 annually, the super contribution is $11,856 (12% of $98,800). This is paid in addition to your gross pay, so your total package is $110,656. The Australian Taxation Office oversees super rules. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. For a gross annual salary of $98,800, the estimated tax is about $18,000, plus Medicare of $1,976, leaving a take-home of around $78,824. This estimate uses the full tax-free threshold and assumes no HELP debt or surcharge. Use our [take-home pay](/). Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and optionally add casual loading. The calculator also shows your fortnightly pay (weekly × 2) and annual gross. It applies the tax and super estimates automatically. For a quick reference, our [reference tables](/data) list common hourly rates and their annual equivalents. Remember that this is an estimate; your actual pay may vary based on enterprise agreements, allowances, or salary packaging.

### Key Takeaways

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assuming 38 hours).
- Casual loading adds 25% on top of the base rate.
- Super is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the contribution cap.
- Tax and Medicare are deducted from gross pay.
- Always check the relevant award pay guide for your minimum entitlements.

For a deeper dive into award rates, visit our [pay guides](/blog) page. If you’re comparing job offers, our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) tool can help you evaluate total remuneration.
